title: turtle-lsp.json
description: Project settings for turtle-lsp, read from turtle-lsp.json at the workspace root by every editor, the command line and CI. Keys may be nested or dotted ("lint.ignore"), optionally inside a top-level "turtle" object.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows.

turtle.description: The same settings, wrapped in a top-level turtle object like the editor's turtle section.

prefixIri.description: The namespace IRI of this prefix.

prefixes.markdownDescription: Prefixes available in every Turtle file, e.g. `{ "ex": "http://example.org/" }`. A `prefixes.ttl` in the project does the same per folder. An editor `prefixes` object replaces these; a dotted key (`"prefixes.ex"`) adds one.
prefixes.description: Prefixes available in every Turtle file, e.g. { "ex": "http://example.org/" }. An editor prefixes object replaces these; a dotted key ("prefixes.ex") adds one.

enumDescriptions: Show labels only for terms whose IRI does not say what they are, such as `ex:P1234`.
Show the label of every term that has one.
inlayHints.labels.description: Which terms get their rdfs:label (or skos:prefLabel) shown as an inlay hint.
inlayHints.labels.markdownDescription: Which terms get their `rdfs:label` (or `skos:prefLabel`) shown as an inlay hint.

shacl.enabled.description: Validate data against the SHACL shapes in the workspace.
shacl.enabled.markdownDescription: Validate data against the SHACL shapes in the workspace.

shacl.maxTriples.description: The most triples one SHACL run validates: the shared Turtle triples plus every dataset (TriG, N-Triples, N-Quads, JSON-LD with named graphs) checked against them. A dataset that would pass the limit is skipped, with a note. This file can lower it but not raise it past 2,000,000: a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.
shacl.maxTriples.markdownDescription: The most triples one SHACL run validates: the shared Turtle triples plus every dataset (TriG, N-Triples, N-Quads, JSON-LD with named graphs) checked against them. A dataset that would pass the limit is skipped, with a note. This file can lower it but not raise it past 2,000,000: a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.

shacl.onType.description: Also validate about a second after you stop typing, on the unsaved text. When off, validation runs on save only.
shacl.onType.markdownDescription: Also validate about a second after you stop typing, on the unsaved text. When off, validation runs on save only.

enumDescriptions: TurbOWL's default OWL 2 RL rules: classes, properties, `owl:sameAs`, property chains and the consistency checks.
Every W3C OWL 2 RL rule. Slower: reasoning takes longer, and so can the proofs hover shows.
reasoning.rules.description: Reason over the workspace's triples, imports included, with TurbOWL, an OWL 2 RL reasoner, in the background. Hover shows a resource's inferred types with their proofs. Its findings become diagnostics with reasoning.diagnostics. This file may choose the rules, except in an untrusted VS Code workspace; reasoning.maxTriples and a 10 s time limit per run still hold.
reasoning.rules.markdownDescription: Reason over the workspace's triples, imports included, with TurbOWL, an OWL 2 RL reasoner, in the background. Hover shows a resource's inferred types with their proofs. Its findings become diagnostics with `reasoning.diagnostics`. This file may choose the rules, except in an untrusted VS Code workspace; `reasoning.maxTriples` and a 10 s time limit per run still hold.

reasoning.maxTriples.description: The most triples reasoning reads: the workspace's and its loaded imports'. Past it, reasoning is skipped, with a note. This file can lower it but not raise it past 2,000,000: a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.
reasoning.maxTriples.markdownDescription: The most triples reasoning reads: the workspace's and its loaded imports'. Past it, reasoning is skipped, with a note. This file can lower it but not raise it past 2,000,000: a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.

reasoning.diagnostics.description: Show TurbOWL's findings (contradictions, ill-typed literals) as diagnostics, each with its proof. Off by default: a project's SHACL shapes often check the same rules, and hover shows the inferred types either way.
reasoning.diagnostics.markdownDescription: Show TurbOWL's findings (contradictions, ill-typed literals) as diagnostics, each with its proof. Off by default: a project's SHACL shapes often check the same rules, and hover shows the inferred types either way.

reasoning.description: OWL 2 RL reasoning with TurbOWL (on by default, with its default rules).
reasoning.markdownDescription: OWL 2 RL reasoning with TurbOWL (on by default, with its default rules).

lint.undescribedTerms.description: Warn about terms in your own namespaces that are used but described nowhere in the workspace. false is the same as listing undescribed-term in lint.ignore.
lint.undescribedTerms.markdownDescription: Warn about terms in your own namespaces that are used but described nowhere in the workspace. `false` is the same as listing `undescribed-term` in `lint.ignore`.

lint.ignore.description: Diagnostic codes never to report, such as unused-prefix or duplicate-label. Adds to the editor's lint.ignore and to --ignore, and wins over lint.enable.
lint.ignore.markdownDescription: Diagnostic codes never to report, such as `unused-prefix` or `duplicate-label`. Adds to the editor's `lint.ignore` and to `--ignore`, and wins over `lint.enable`.

lint.enable.description: Off-by-default checks to switch on: missing-label, missing-definition, multiple-definitions, duplicate-definition, lowercase-definition, missing-ontology-title, missing-ontology-description and missing-ontology-license. Adds to the editor's lint.enable. A code in lint.ignore stays off.
lint.enable.markdownDescription: Off-by-default checks to switch on: `missing-label`, `missing-definition`, `multiple-definitions`, `duplicate-definition`, `lowercase-definition`, `missing-ontology-title`, `missing-ontology-description` and `missing-ontology-license`. Adds to the editor's `lint.enable`. A code in `lint.ignore` stays off.

imports.network.description: Fetch owl:imports and remote JSON-LD contexts that are not in the workspace over the network. This file cannot turn it on: true is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Turn it on in the editor's settings or with --network.
imports.network.markdownDescription: Fetch `owl:imports` and remote JSON-LD contexts that are not in the workspace over the network. This file cannot turn it on: `true` is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Turn it on in the editor's settings or with `--network`.

enumDescriptions: Show SHACL results that the missing data could change as warnings, with a note naming the imports.
Treat unresolved imports as empty: SHACL results keep their full severity and get no note.
imports.unresolved.description: How SHACL validation treats owl:imports that are not loaded. Either way, each unresolved import keeps its information diagnostic.
imports.unresolved.markdownDescription: How SHACL validation treats `owl:imports` that are not loaded. Either way, each unresolved import keeps its information diagnostic.

diagnostics.workspace.description: Show problems in every workspace file, not only the open ones. Files that are not open are checked in the background, as turtle-lsp check checks them, and again when they change on disk.
diagnostics.workspace.markdownDescription: Show problems in every workspace file, not only the open ones. Files that are not open are checked in the background, as `turtle-lsp check` checks them, and again when they change on disk.

parse.incremental.description: After an edit, parse only the statements around it instead of the whole file. The results are the same either way. The command line always parses whole files.
parse.incremental.markdownDescription: After an edit, parse only the statements around it instead of the whole file. The results are the same either way. The command line always parses whole files.

format.lineWidth.description: Line width the formatter aims for.
format.lineWidth.markdownDescription: Line width the formatter aims for.

codeLens.references.description: Show the number of references above each subject a file describes. Click it to list the references.
codeLens.references.markdownDescription: Show the number of references above each subject a file describes. Click it to list the references.

query.timeoutSeconds.description: Stop a query run with ▶ Run query or turtle-lsp query after this many seconds. This file can lower it but not raise it past 30 (0, no limit, counts as past): a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.
query.timeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Stop a query run with **▶ Run query** or `turtle-lsp query` after this many seconds. This file can lower it but not raise it past 30 (`0`, no limit, counts as past): a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.

query.maxRows.description: Show at most this many rows (or triples) of a query's results; the total is still counted. This file can lower it but not raise it past 1,000 (0, no limit, counts as past): a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.
query.maxRows.markdownDescription: Show at most this many rows (or triples) of a query's results; the total is still counted. This file can lower it but not raise it past 1,000 (`0`, no limit, counts as past): a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.

query.maxBufferedRows.description: Stop a query that keeps more than this many rows in memory to sort, group, deduplicate or join them (ordinary rows take about 100 bytes each; long text values take more). This file can lower it but not raise it past 10,000,000 (0, no limit, counts as past): a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.
query.maxBufferedRows.markdownDescription: Stop a query that keeps more than this many rows in memory to sort, group, deduplicate or join them (ordinary rows take about 100 bytes each; long text values take more). This file can lower it but not raise it past 10,000,000 (`0`, no limit, counts as past): a larger value is ignored with a warning, since any repository you clone can ship the file. Raise it in the editor's settings or with a command-line flag.

enumDescriptions: Only the written triples, as without reasoning.
Also the triples TurbOWL infers with its default OWL 2 RL rules.
Also the triples TurbOWL infers with every W3C OWL 2 RL rule. Slower.
query.reasoning.description: Run queries with ▶ Run query over the triples TurbOWL infers from the workspace, imports' axioms included, as well as the written ones. The results say how many inferred triples they include. Apart from reasoning.rules. This file may choose it; reasoning.maxTriples still holds.
query.reasoning.markdownDescription: Run queries with **▶ Run query** over the triples TurbOWL infers from the workspace, imports' axioms included, as well as the written ones. The results say how many inferred triples they include. Apart from `reasoning.rules`. This file may choose it; `reasoning.maxTriples` still holds.

query.description: SPARQL query runs: their limits, which this file can lower but not raise, and their inferred triples.
query.markdownDescription: SPARQL query runs: their limits, which this file can lower but not raise, and their inferred triples.
